name: Deerhoof
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: A kitchen-table San Francisco noise trio that became a shape-shifting pop band, then opened for Radiohead, played CERN and quit Spotify.

eras.title: A bass, a harmonica and a week
eras.text: A San Francisco solo project turns into a noise trio with a singer who had never been in a band. Kill Rock Stars signs them almost on sight.

years.src: Wikipedia: Deerhoof · Wikipedia: Greg Saunier · Life of the Record
years.h: Rob Fisk starts Deerhoof; Greg Saunier shows up a week later
years.p: [[Rob Fisk|0eedfcc1-da57-4c7a-99c7-7a51b31f1be0]] began Deerhoof in San Francisco as a bass and harmonica solo project. Drummer [[Greg Saunier|2ae4e9b4-9e8b-4a98-920d-4f3a881dac96]] joined about a week later.
years.xp:
Saunier, a 1991 Oberlin Conservatory graduate, had been drumming in a San Francisco band called Nitre Pit. When its guitarists left, he and Fisk kept the name going for the remaining shows as a much stranger, stripped-down duo, according to Wikipedia's account of Saunier's career.

Fisk later recalled the early band practicing in a kitchen with almost no equipment.

years.h: Slim Moon sees them at Yoyo A Go Go and signs them to Kill Rock Stars
years.p: Kill Rock Stars founder Slim Moon caught the duo at the 1994 Yoyo A Go Go festival, and the label released Deerhoof's records through 2008's Offend Maggie.

years.src: Wikipedia: Deerhoof · Life of the Record
years.h: Satomi Matsuzaki lands from Japan and joins within a week
years.p: [[Satomi Matsuzaki|c46e7f09-6ed4-42e7-b927-86d42929bb69]] moved to the United States, joined [[Deerhoof|11eabe0c-2638-4808-92f9-1dbd9c453429]] within a week with no band experience, and went on tour as its singer a week after that, opening for Caroliner.
years.xp: Matsuzaki has said she thought she was joining a noise band, which then turned into a rock band. Her voice, bright and unguarded against Saunier's drumming and Fisk's bass, became the thing people describe first when they describe the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Man, the King, the Girl
years.h: The Man, the King, the Girl arrives on Kill Rock Stars
years.p: Recorded on a 4-track, it pairs twelve studio songs with five live tracks, including the instrumentals "Gold on Black" and "Tiger Chain." Fisk, Matsuzaki and Saunier are the trio.
years.xp: The record came out on October 28, 1997 through Kill Rock Stars and 5 Rue Christine. Matsuzaki, who also drew Deerhoof's covers, is the singer.
play: The Man, the King, the Girl

eras.title: Fisk out, Dieterich in
eras.text: A keyboard player comes and goes, the founding bassist leaves, and a guitarist arrives who will still be here a quarter century later.

years.h: Kelly Goode joins on keyboards
years.p: [[Kelly Goode|f4fbb7a4-1db8-4c04-8290-7eb129f2da33]] became the first player added to the trio, bringing keyboards into the noise.

years.h: Holdypaws gets Xiu Xiu's Jamie Stewart listening
years.p: Self-produced and released on Kill Rock Stars. Jamie Stewart of [[Xiu Xiu|8b431ac6-0806-4e4a-9b6b-1734370fa890]] said he had never heard anything like it and that it changed how he thought about music.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 5.7 out of 10, so the record split critics from the start. Henry Rollins, who praised Deerhoof and the later Green Cosmos EP, was among the more vocal fans, saying the music gets the blood going.

years.h: Fisk and Goode leave to form 7 Year Rabbit Cycle
years.p: Founding bassist Rob Fisk and keyboardist Kelly Goode left in 1999. [[John Dieterich|f368404c-789e-4659-a17f-d21c9a091dc1]] joined on guitar afterward.
years.xp:
Encyclopedia.com reports the two left together to start 7 Year Rabbit Cycle.

Dieterich, Matsuzaki and Saunier would stay together, with only guitarists changing, for the next quarter century.

eras.title: Cats, cassettes and a breakthrough
eras.text: With Dieterich and a new guitarist, Deerhoof gets faster, sweeter and more precise. Critics start paying attention.

years.h: Reveille is a 33-minute trio record
years.p: Matsuzaki plays bass, Dieterich guitar and Saunier drums on the record that gets Deerhoof its first big reviews. Pitchfork gave it 8.5.
years.xp: Released on Kill Rock Stars and 5 Rue Christine, the album has a cover designed by Matsuzaki. [[Chris Cohen|d06cbcab-2094-4b51-9ccf-f4af33494ef1]] plays guitar on a single track.

years.h: [[Chris Cohen|d06cbcab-2094-4b51-9ccf-f4af33494ef1]] sneaks in as a fourth member
years.p: Between the completion and release of Reveille, Cohen became Deerhoof's second guitarist. Matsuzaki says he "snuck in" by coming to shows and contributing songs.

years.h: Apple O' earns Pitchfork's Best New Music
years.p: Chris Cohen's first record as a member. Pitchfork ranked it 16th among its top albums of 2003 and 199th among the best of the decade.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that Karen O picked it for Rolling Stone's 2003 Music Awards and that the band quit their day jobs to tour. The album's extensive touring bought Deerhoof an international audience.

years.h: Milk Man is a concept piece with a cover character
years.p: The character on the sleeve was drawn by Ken Kagami, a friend and former housemate. Pitchfork gave it 7.6.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com says the record drew Beck and Stephen Malkmus in as fans. Wikipedia says it sat at No. 1 on the Dusted radio chart for six weeks, though that is a single-source claim.

eras.title: Nine to five in Oakland
eras.text: A double album, a tour with Radiohead, and the end of the four-piece.

years.h: Green Cosmos EP
years.p: A mini-album on Kill Rock Stars that mixes orchestral sound with dance music.

years.src: Life of the Record · Wikipedia: The Runners Four
years.h: The Runners Four, recorded like a day job
years.p: Twenty tracks, each member taking a turn as singer. The band worked at an Oakland rehearsal space called Soundwave from nine to five for about eight months.
years.xp:
Saunier told Life of the Record about a 13-hour stretch in front of Pro Tools without leaving his chair. He also said that on a good system, after mixing it against Queens of the Stone Age, the record sounded scrawny to him.

Pitchfork gave it 9.0.

years.big: Nine to five, in a windowless room
q: I often feel that I missed my twenties.
years.h: Eight months of work weeks
years.p: Saunier says the process left him feeling he had lost his twenties to computer screens. Chris Cohen said there was no going back to the earlier, more carefree time.
years.xp: The band recorded Monday to Friday like employees, and both Saunier and Cohen say it strained things. Cohen said it was not a success in a personal way.

years.cap: Deerhoof playing at Prospect Park in Brooklyn · Wikimedia
years.src: Drowned in Sound · Concert Archives · DIY
years.h: Opening for Radiohead, and Thom Yorke shows up in Dublin
years.p: Deerhoof supported [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] across the US and Europe. Guitarist Ed O'Brien asked how to steal their tone, and Jonny Greenwood lit their Amsterdam show without telling them.
years.xp:
According to Drowned in Sound, Colin Greenwood apologized for missing an Oxford show, and in Dublin Thom Yorke skipped a traditional music gig to watch Deerhoof, arriving sweaty from dancing. Radiohead's sound engineer Jim Warren mixed their European dates for free.

The dates fell during the band's Runners Four tour cycle, and at least one Los Angeles date is listed for June 30, 2006 at the Greek Theatre.

years.h: Chris Cohen leaves after a film score and a Danielson record
years.p: His last work with Deerhoof was a live score for Harry Smith's Heaven and Earth Magic. The band also backed Danielson on Ships.

years.h: Friend Opportunity ships with twelve different covers
years.p: British artist David Shrigley made twelve front covers. It's a trio record: Dieterich, Matsuzaki, Saunier.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 8.9 and The A.V. Club an A minus. It peaked at No. 3 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.

eras.title: Four again, and a new label
eras.text: Ed Rodriguez fills the empty guitar chair, the band leaves Kill Rock Stars, and Deerhoof turns into a self-recording, online-releasing machine.

years.h: Ed Rodriguez joins from Gorge Trio
years.p: [[Ed Rodriguez|b88667bb-99ae-4635-a2a3-d311d59e2b8b]], who also played in [[Gorge Trio|de6800f2-ae5e-4e28-ba3b-1ee3b46b6fd9]] and XBXRX, made Deerhoof a quartet again.

years.h: Offend Maggie hands Rodriguez his first songs
years.p: Metacritic scored it 80. The band invited fans to record their own versions of "Fresh Born" from sheet music posted online.

years.h: The Flaming Lips ask Deerhoof to play All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: At the New York festival, [[The Flaming Lips|1f43d76f-8edf-44f6-aaf1-b65f05ad9402]] singer Wayne Coyne told Saunier he was a master of spazzing out intuitively.
years.xp: Saunier says Coyne's first question backstage was how the band had written "Sirius Star."

years.h: Deerhoof plays Unknown Pleasures with Xiu Xiu
years.p: With [[Xiu Xiu|8b431ac6-0806-4e4a-9b6b-1734370fa890]], the band performed Joy Division's whole Unknown Pleasures at Donaufestival in Austria and on the Brooklyn waterfront.

years.h: Deerhoof vs. Evil is released one track at a time
years.p: "The Merry Barracks" premiered on Pitchfork on October 8, 2010, then the rest rolled out across different websites before the full album appeared on Polyvinyl Records.

years.h: Breakup Song is a flexi-book
years.p: Released on Polyvinyl and Joyful Noise Recordings, it lets listeners flip from song to song like pages in a storybook.
years.xp: The band wrote it because they felt breakup songs are usually too sad. That October they put out the single "Sexy, but Sparkly" with Chris Shaw, their first time with an outside producer.

years.h: La Isla Bonita starts as an argument over Joan Jett or Janet Jackson
years.p: Made at guitarist Ed Rodriguez's home. Its lead single "Exit Only" grew out of a live cover of the Ramones' "Pinhead."
years.xp: Wikipedia says demos were cut at Rodriguez's Oregon home with producer Nick Sylvester. Matsuzaki told Vice they recorded in Ed's basement over ten days in a really small room.

eras.title: Particle physics, arenas and a Spotify exit
eras.text: Deerhoof plays CERN, opens for Red Hot Chili Peppers, makes a concept record, and takes its music off the biggest streaming service.

years.h: First band to play CERN's Large Hadron Collider
years.p: Deerhoof was the first act invited to perform at CERN for the Ex/Noise/CERN project.
years.xp: Physicist James Beacham said musical curiosity is like scientific curiosity, and that Deerhoof has inspired him as much as Einstein.

years.h: The Magic becomes their first CMJ No. 1
years.p: It blends glam metal, punk and noise, and includes a cover of The Ink Spots' "I Don't Want to Set the World on Fire."

years.h: Opening arenas for the Red Hot Chili Peppers in a Prius
years.p: The band trailed the Chili Peppers' buses and trucks through northern Europe in a Prius minivan.
years.xp: Saunier told Stereogum the shows forced them to rethink everything, since reverb in a 20,000-seat arena turns a snare hit to mud.

years.h: Mountain Moves is a protest record with guests
years.p: Guests include Awkwafina, Jenn Wasner, Juana Molina and Lætitia Sadier. Early Bandcamp sales benefited the Emergent Fund.

years.h: Future Teenage Cave Artists, a first concept record
years.p: Wikipedia calls it the band's first overt concept album.

years.h: Miracle-Level is sung entirely in Japanese
years.p: Recorded in about two weeks at No Fun Club in Winnipeg. Pitchfork gave it 7.9.

years.src: Wikipedia: Noble and Godlike in Ruin
years.h: Noble and Godlike in Ruin is a "Deerhoofstein"
years.p: Saunier calls the album their low-budget DIY Frankenstein. Its cover stitches band faces together.

q: We don't want our music killing people.
years.h: Deerhoof removes its catalog from Spotify
years.p: Deerhoof announced it would pull its music from Spotify over CEO Daniel Ek's investment in Helsing, a German defense AI company.
years.xp: MusicRadar reported the band said it earns more from touring than streaming. BrooklynVegan and the SF Chronicle covered the exit.
